## Example 3.23 {#fv6-example-3-23 .fv-lesson .circle-lesson }

```{=html}
<p>Sketch the locus <span data-math="|\underset{\sim}{r}-\underset{\sim}{p}|=\lambda"></span>,</p><div class="fv-equation"><span data-math="\text{where }\underset{\sim}{r}=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix},\quad \underset{\sim}{p}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\4\end{bmatrix}\quad\text{and }\lambda=5."></span></div><p>Clearly label the centre and radius.</p>
```

<div class="booklet-cue">Booklet Example 3.23 · p. 72</div>

::: {.notes}
OneNote: (x−3)²+(y−4)²=25. Centre (3,4), radius 5. Equal scale on the axes. Useful extremal points (−2,4), (8,4), (3,−1), (3,9). If intercepts are useful: (0,0), (6,0), (0,8), but these are not required by the question. Keep the plotted circle round and avoid judging the radius from an uneven axis scale.
:::
